decision.summary: The Fed raised its policy rate by 25 basis points, to 5.25%. The vote was 10-0.

changes.quote: The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to raise its target for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 5-1/4 percent.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to raise its target for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 5 percent.”

changes.quote: Recent indicators suggest that economic growth is moderating from its quite strong pace earlier this year, partly reflecting a gradual cooling of the housing market and the lagged effects of increases in interest rates and energy prices.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: Readings on core inflation have been elevated in recent months.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: Ongoing productivity gains have held down the rise in unit labor costs, and inflation expectations remain contained.

changes.quote: However, the high levels of resource utilization and of the prices of energy and other commodities have the potential to sustain inflation pressures.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Still, possible increases in resource utilization, in combination with the elevated prices of energy and other commodities, have the potential to add to inflati…”

changes.quote: Although the moderation in the growth of aggregate demand should help to limit inflation pressures over time, the Committee judges that some inflation risks remain.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

tone_quotes.quote: The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to raise its target for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 5-1/4 percent.

The extent and timing of any additional firming that may be needed to address these risks will depend on the evolution of the outlook for both inflation and economic growth, as implied by incoming information.
However, the high levels of resource utilization and of the prices of energy and other commodities have the potential to sustain inflation pressures.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 13.3% APR, a 25 bp increase raises monthly interest by about $1.04.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 5.22% and moved -3 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 6.71% would fall by about $5.97 a month.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $15.00 a year more in interest.
Unemployment was 4.6%, and employers added an average of 172k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 4% over the past year (May 2006); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 2.4%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 5.5% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -8 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.18% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is hawkish (leaning toward higher rates). The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 10%, cut 0%, hike 90%.
